newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean yields close lower on abundant liquidity.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean yields close lower on abundant liquidity.

text.p: Active buying interest on the back of fluid short-term liquidity and improving macro-economic indicators pushed yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds to close lower on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Both short- and long-term yields closed lower aided by extensive buying interest, while short-term liquidity remained ample," said a LG Securities dealer.
But trading volume was thin in the absence of sellers.
Dealers said corporate money demand was low and banks remained cash rich after insurers deposited premiums received from their clients.
The first monthly trade surplus in 30 months and stabilised inflation also caused healthy buying interest, pushing corporate yields down.

Of 54 billion won worth of new corporate bond issuances on Wednesday, 50 billion won worth was not guaranteed. Dealers said this reflected the recent trend for financial institutions to be reluctant to guarantee payment of bonds.
"Yesterday was the turning point for interest rates. With improving liquidity among non-banking financial institutions, the rates will show a gradual decline."
But the LG Securities dealer said the yields would consolidate after falling to 11.45 percent.
"From a technical point of view, further sharp declines will be limited," he said.
Tax payments valued at about 1.2 trillion won were almost balanced with redemption of one trillion won repurchase agreement by the central bank.
CDs and overnight call rate also fell in line with improving market liquidity, dealers said.
